html:
On 1 December 1948 José Figueres announced that Costa Rica would abolish its army, and Article 12 of the constitution of 1949 made it law. Only police and coast guard forces remain.

Figueres had just won the civil war, and the army was a threat to any government. He struck a wall of the army headquarters with a hammer, and the building became the national museum. The money saved went into schools, health and the social security system built by Calderón Guardia.

Costa Rica has relied since then on treaties and the Organization of American States for defence. While its neighbours suffered coups and Cold War civil wars, it stayed a democracy, and 1 December is now a public holiday. It is one of very few countries in the world with no army.
sum: On 1 December 1948 José Figueres announced that Costa Rica would abolish its army, and Article 12 of the constitution of 1949 made it law. Only police and coast guard forces remain.
